title: I'm Nobody! Who are you?
author: Emily Dickinson
edition: Poems by Emily Dickinson, Series Two (1891), ed. T. W. Higginson and Mabel Loomis Todd - Part One: Life, poem I. Original spacing "there 's" / "they 'd" closed up to "there's" / "they'd".
source: Project Gutenberg eBook 2679, 'Poems by Emily Dickinson, Series Two', https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2679/pg2679.txt (lines 233-241), retrieved 2026-10-11. Public domain in the US. NOTE: the LibriVox page itself cites https://www.bartleby.com/113/1027.html, which returns HTTP 403 to automated requests; Gutenberg was used instead and is the same 1891 Todd/Higginson text.
verbatim: I'm nobody! Who are you? Are you nobody, too? Then there's a pair of us -- don't tell! They'd banish us, you know. How dreary to be somebody! How public, like a frog To tell your name the livelong day To an admiring bog!
display:
I'm nobody! Who are you? Are you nobody, too? Then there's a pair of us -- don't tell! They'd banish us, you know.

How dreary to be somebody! How public, like a frog To tell your name the livelong day To an admiring bog!
notes: 17 readers (S5) - the largest envelope in the dataset.
TODO(human) - EDITION VARIANT, affects most readers. This 1891 edition reads
'To tell your name the livelong DAY'. The modern Johnson/Franklin text reads
'the livelong JUNE', and that is the wording most people know. Readers will
have used either, so this one word needs checking per file and an override
for every reader who says 'June'. Check this before aligning anything.
WARNING - LENGTH. The poem is 8 lines / 40 tokens, so each reading is only
~20-25 s of speech. That is far shorter than s1_gettysburg (272 tokens) and
gives few words and few gaps per rendition, so per-word envelope statistics
here rest on 17 readings of 40 words rather than on a long text. Useful for
leave-one-text-out as a genuinely independent text, but do not expect it to
carry region-level detection on its own.
ENVELOPE NOTE (spec 10.1): readers who deviate from the edition in `source`
need their own dataset/texts/overrides/<file_id>.txt, and a reading with an
override has a different word sequence from the 1891 edition, so word i is not
comparable across the two. Decide per text whether to drop deviating takes or
to align word sequences across renditions first.
LibriVox INTRO/OUTRO: every file in this collection opens with a spoken
LibriVox disclaimer and reader credit and closes with an end announcement, none
of which is part of this text. excerpt_start_s / excerpt_end_s are still null in
SOURCES.yaml for every file, so until they are set per file, MFA will try to
align the disclaimer against this text and scripts/align_report.py will flag all
of them. This is the single biggest remaining job for this text.
